file_description: Historical Gas Wells (Pre-2009) - Monthly well count by status and type for gas fields
data_format: LONG format - multiple rows per field-month, one per well type and status concept
priority: LOW - Historical data, useful for long-term trend analysis but not critical for recent operations
use_case: Historical well count trends, operator consolidation history, long-term field development patterns

field_descriptions.well_count: Number of wells in the specified status category for the field-month. Integer count.
field_descriptions.well_type: Primary well classification: producing wells vs injection/EOR wells
field_descriptions.status_concept: Specific operational status or reason for well state
field_descriptions.field_name: Field name (yacimiento) - note: no field_id in historical data, matching to modern data requires name matching
field_descriptions.data_date: Date stamp of data entry - end of month

status_concept_descriptions.active_production: Wells actively producing gas - flowing naturally or with artificial lift. Contributing to monthly production.
status_concept_descriptions.temporarily_shut_in: Wells temporarily shut in - capable of production but not currently flowing. Reasons: maintenance, equipment issues, market conditions, regulatory.
status_concept_descriptions.remote_areas_no_infrastructure: Wells in remote areas lacking pipeline infrastructure or gathering facilities. May be capable of production but cannot deliver gas to market.
status_concept_descriptions.shut_in_reserve: Wells drilled and completed but held in reserve - not producing. Economic or strategic reasons for keeping shut in.
status_concept_descriptions.reserve_for_secondary_eor: Wells drilled for future use in secondary recovery or EOR operations. Not currently being used for production or injection.
status_concept_descriptions.other_inactive_reasons: Wells inactive for other unspecified reasons. May include: regulatory restrictions, legal disputes, technical issues, or pending decisions.
status_concept_descriptions.water_injection_active: Wells actively injecting water for secondary recovery (waterflooding) or pressure maintenance. Not producing.
status_concept_descriptions.gas_injection_active: Wells actively injecting gas for pressure maintenance, gas cycling in condensate reservoirs, or gas cap maintenance.
status_concept_descriptions.pressure_maintenance_injection: Wells used for pressure maintenance - may include water, gas, or other fluid injection to support reservoir pressure and oil/gas production.

well_type_descriptions.gas_producing_wells: Wells primarily drilled and completed for gas production. May be producing, shut-in, or in reserve status.
well_type_descriptions.secondary_eor_wells: Wells used for secondary recovery (waterflooding) or enhanced oil recovery (EOR) operations. Includes active injectors and wells held in reserve for future injection.

unit_notes.well_count: Integer count of wells - not production volumes
unit_notes.aggregation: Counts are per field per month. Sum across concepts for total well count.
unit_notes.no_production_data: This file contains well counts only, not production volumes or rates

data_quality_notes.no_field_id: Historical data lacks field_id. Must match to modern data using field_name string matching. Field names may have changed over time.
data_quality_notes.company_name_changes: Company names from 1999-2008 reflect historical ownership. Many companies have merged, been acquired, or changed names.
data_quality_notes.data_completeness: Pre-2009 data may have gaps or inconsistencies. Data collection standards improved in later years.
data_quality_notes.concept_evolution: Status concepts in historical data may not perfectly match modern classifications.
data_quality_notes.zero_vs_null: Zero well count may mean: (1) no wells in that status, (2) field not active that month, (3) data not reported.

calculated_metrics.total_wells_per_field_month: SUM(well_count) across all concepts for field-month
calculated_metrics.active_fraction: active_production_count / total_well_count - fraction of wells producing
calculated_metrics.producer_to_injector_ratio: active_production_count / injector_count - indicates secondary recovery intensity

technical_notes.historical_context: 1999-2008 was pre-Vaca Muerta era - mostly conventional production. Unconventional shale development began ~2010.
technical_notes.data_vintage: This data is 15-25 years old. Well counts and operators have changed significantly. Use primarily for historical trend analysis.
technical_notes.operator_consolidation: Many operators from 1999-2008 no longer exist. Industry consolidation has occurred. YPF, Pluspetrol, Total, Shell, Pan American Energy are key players across eras.
technical_notes.well_count_vs_production: Well count alone doesn't indicate production levels. One high-rate well may outproduce 10 low-rate wells.
technical_notes.inactive_well_costs: High shutin/reserve counts indicate high well carrying costs and potential reactivation opportunities.
technical_notes.injection_well_importance: Active injection well count indicates maturity of secondary recovery operations. More injectors = more mature waterflood.

data_integration.matching_challenge: No field_id in historical data. Must match to modern field database using field_name string matching with fuzzy logic.
data_integration.time_gap: This data ends at 2008. Modern well production data starts 2009. There's no overlap for validation.
data_integration.use_for_trends: Best use: long-term field development trends, historical operator activity, well count evolution over 1999-2008 period.
data_integration.supplementary_only: Treat as supplementary historical context, not primary data source for current operations.

use_cases.historical_trends: Analyze field development history, well count growth patterns from 1999-2008
use_cases.operator_history: Track historical operator presence and consolidation patterns
use_cases.field_maturity: Identify fields with long production history vs newer developments
use_cases.shutin_analysis: Historical shutin patterns may indicate chronic issues or market dynamics
use_cases.limited_value_for_current: Low priority for current emissions/operations analysis - data too old

limitations.outdated: Data is 15-25 years old - operators, field names, and well counts have changed significantly
limitations.no_field_id: Cannot directly join to modern data without name matching and validation
limitations.no_production_volumes: Well counts only - no production rates or volumes
limitations.no_well_ids: Cannot track individual wells - only aggregate counts by status
limitations.inconsistent_concepts: Status concepts may not align perfectly with modern classification system
limitations.low_priority: Low value for near-term operations, emissions estimation, or current field analysis

example_analysis.field_name_matching_python: from fuzzywuzzy import fuzz; best_match = max(modern_fields, key=lambda x: fuzz.ratio(historical_name, x))
